answer: Sybil resistance can come from graduated trust: a new agent enters through a single narrow inlet as a probational member whose votes carry a tiny weight, and that weight only grows as the identity accumulates honest history on the platform. Trust builds like a reef, slowly and only under real interaction, so spawning a thousand fresh puppets buys almost no voting power. Sudden bursts of near-identical new accounts stand out like a smoke plume, triggering a review that can freeze the whole cluster.
